questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had been in Switzerland three times before my departure, why I was in love with Switzerland even before. And now I love Switzerland even more. The three times I was there before, it was only on vacation, why I didn't have time to explore the whole country. Therefore, I wanted to have more time in Switzerland to explore the whole country. Switzerland is very unique in every aspect. Sometimes you don't believe that it is a part of Europe. The fact that it is so different from the other counties in Europe is one of the main reasons why I chose Switzerland. A lot of the counties in Europe are so similar to Denmark, why going on an exchange doesn't change that much. However, the situation is different with Switzerland. Everything is turned upside down in Switzerland. The system is different. The people are different. There are 4 main languages and English is not one of them. The University is different. The nature is unique and different. The food is unique and different. Everything is different, which makes it interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I will give the study abroad 9/10, because I will leave some space for some improvements. It could have been made a little bit easier in terms of paperwork and/or moving exams to Denmark, for instance. The experience was 10/10, but some pratical things were a bit stressful, why the overall rate is 9/10.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Bern sends you all the information you need by email. There is a lot of information you receive, and they require that you read everything before your arrival. It's very pratical information about the introduction week, how to register to courses, how to change courses etc etc. Furthermore, there is a zoom meeting, where they are going through all the information step by step. It's also possible to ask questions there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There is an introduction week, where they provide you with all the information you need. However, it's just pratical information, which you knew before if you read the information you received by email roughly. However, they are well organized and very helpful. And if you need any further information or help, they are always free and ready to help at their office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very professional.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I have a family member, who lives in Switzerland. Therefore, I lived at their place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I had some friends (that I meet there), which lived in a student lodge (Bumpliz Nord). The Student lodge was very popular. My friends lived with other exchange students, why they also meet more people from the University than I did. I lived in private accommodation, why I had to meet people through introduction week, sports and/or courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't look for any housing, since I lived with a family member there. However, I never heard anyone say anything bad about it, why I give it 4. A lot of the people that I hang out with there lived in a student lodge, which seemed to be open for everybody.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration system is different from what we are used to in Denmark. You need to read the information carefully, and use some time to learn to use the system. However, they provide you with all the information, and it's not that difficult.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They use to systems. One system is a webside called KSL. In KSL you can read about all the courses in Switzerland, register to courses, deregister from courses, receive grades etc. The other system is Illias, which is where you can see the courses you have registered for. Illias is very similar to absalon, which is used a lot in Denmark. This is the platform where you can see your chosen courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The University is always ready to help if you have any kind of questions. This can be given through zoom or email if before arrival, or you can ask in the office at your stay there. Above that, there is always a lot of other people in the same situation, which are ready to help if you have any questions are your stay.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I read about all the courses at the University of Bern quite early. Therefore I had a good idea which courses I wanted to participate in. However, the University of Bern offers students to change courses throughout the semester, why I changed some courses along the way. This is not recommended, but it's easy to change courses if you want throughout the semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to check the structure of the courses. As an exchange student you want to have time to do other things (apart from studying) as well. I would check (for instance) if there is any required tasks you need to do, what time of the day the lecture is (make sure not to have some at the same time), when the exams are (they are quite close in Bern), how the exam is (written/oral/presentation) etc etc. Thereafter, I would choose the courses that fits best your preferences.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was good. However, there could be some improvements. Some things were better at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses where quite similar to the level of the University of Copenhagen. However, most of the courses are only 4.5 ECTS compared to 7.5 ECTS at the University of Copenhagen, why you need to take more course to achieve 30 ECTS.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was quite similar to that of UCPH. The structure was the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Banking theory (4.5 ECTS)
2. Combinatorial Optimization (4.5 ECTS)
3. Macroeconomics II (4.5 ECTS)
4. Mathematical Methods in Economics (4.5 ECTS)
5. Microeconomics II (4.5 ECTS)
6. Organization Behavior (4.5 ECTS)
7. Organization Economics (4.5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Banking theory, Macroeconomics II (if you liked macroeconomics III at KU), Microeconomics II, Organizational Economics and Organizational Behavior. You might notice that this is all course with pen and paper math only. If you like pen and paper math, I would recommend this. There is no required taks you need to pass during this courses, only the exam, which is an written exam at the end of the semester. Banking theory might have some midterm exam, which was not the case during my stay. Organizational Behavior is not math, but rather how people behave, which is very interesting, and the exam is an multiple choice exam at the end of the semester.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Switzerland is very expensive, that should not come as an surprise. However, I was surprised about how expensive the local transportation and car parking was. I had a car with me, and the parking was so high that I was not able to use the car inside the city (Sometimes I did, but not every day). Therefore I bought a monthly train travel card, which gave me free access to travel inside an area around Bern (via busses, metros, trains etc). However, I had to pay around 2.100 DKK for this travel card every month. Therefore, I would say that transportation cost is expensive in Switzerland. However, I think it's possible to get it much cheaper than I did. I bought all zones, since I lived 30min. away from Bern., and I did not use the half-fare opportunity, which is recommended by everybody.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think the local supermarkets (like. Coop, Migros and more) were less expensive that I expected. The reason is that I expected everything to be extremely expensive before departure. However, the big supermarkets produce food/items for some fair prices. On the other side, is it very expensive to go out for shopping, eating on restaurants, cafés etc.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was on of the best part of the exchange. The University of Bern offers to many opportunities for exchange students. Very impressive. For instance, they offer more than 100 different sports activities for students for free. The only thing you need to do is to register. There is no limit for all the activities. Very enjoyable and easy to meet a lot of other people through this opportunity. This is something that every country, and every University in the world should learn from (The University of Copenhagen included).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many different cultural, athletic and social activities available that it's impossible to write them all down. There are more than 100 different sport activities plus a lot of cultural and athletic activities going on all the time, it's absolutely breathtaking. It's actually easier for me to say what is not there, because everything else it there. Therefore I would say that the only thing that I missed was some place to play paddle tennis and a bigger climbing hall. Otherwise I think you can do everything else there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are so many beautiful things to do in Switzerland. Hiking, skiing, visit different cities/places (so many beautiful places), visit the parlament, visit some chokolade production, visit some cheese production, visit some vine production, swim in Aare etc etc. There are so many different opportunities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around Switzerland. There are so many beautiful places. For example explore and visit the cities Bern, Zurich, Geneve, Lausanne and all small beautiful places around Bern (for example Grindewald, Murren, Wengen, Interlaken, Oeschinensee etc.)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. The people are very helpful and easy going. They are very similar to Danes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just go ahead and ask a lot of questions. They are very nice to talk to, and very helpful.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any cultural differences particularly challenging. The only thing that was a bit challenging was to understand 4 different languages. However, it was just a positive challenge to try to understand the people there.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The way the people treat each other was the part that I appreciated the most. I think the people are so nice to each other there. If you have a question, they don't just answer the question, they also follow up upon the question. You can feel the love from the people there. They are very welcoming, interested in you and helpful. That was my experience. For me, it felt like a culture where people were helping each other all the time. They didn't seem so stressed, but rather more smiling and taking their time to help others.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be social and open (Participate in sports, hiking, skiing etc.), enjoy the semester (don't think too much about grades etc.), try to learn a new (local) language (it's fun).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy your stay, ask a lot of questions and meet a lot of interesting people along the way.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The sports program, meeting new people, learning new language, hiking and visiting new places.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams and learning a new language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
